checks.result: Correct under the stated common posted-offer protocol, participation at equality, quality-independent splitting, sufficient funds and no capacity limit. Zero profit is explicitly only a candidate test. Alpha1/3 implies low-only p6; raising a single buyer's offer above6 either buys L at a loss or both types at expected value10 below their admission price12. Alpha3/4 gives all-trade p15 and the p13 deviation against p6 earns2. At alpha1/2 both p6 and p12 survive weak best responses because an offer12 against p6 yields zero rather than positive profit. The manuscript appropriately does not infer uniqueness at equality.

Checked 81 quarter-dollar offers from0 to20 for each of four candidates (alpha1/3,p6; alpha3/4,p15; alpha1/2,p6; alpha1/2,p12), with maximum deviation profit0 throughout; separately p13 against alpha3/4,p6 yields2. Reviewed the written all-price intervals, which carry the continuous claim beyond this grid.

checks.result: The signaling-game PBE definition is deliberately scoped. Atom Bayes formulas are not misapplied to continuous mixed draws. Employer expected productivity4+6mu is supported by an explicit competing-bid continuation after every signal, including off path. All type deviations are checked globally under the stated wage schedule. Separating signals satisfy2<=s<=6, with weak endpoint incentives; pooling at zero works for off-path mu0 but fails for mu1/2. Refinement discussion is motivation for an added restriction, not an assertion that Bayes alone fixes unused-signal beliefs.
checks.independent_calculation: Checked employer deviations directly: against a rival wage equal to value, a lower bid loses, a tie yields zero and a higher bid earns negative expected profit. Used 13 beliefs k/12 and 50 listed bids per belief (including the exact equilibrium value). Separately evaluated low/high signal payoff functions at s2,3,6 against an exact finite signal grid plus each on-path signal, and reviewed the global bound that every other signal pays4 and adds nonnegative cost. Recomputed s1 low deviation7>4, s7 high deviation4>3, pooling deviation ranges e<1 and e<1/3, and e2 refinement comparisons4<6<8. Expected net outputs at s2 ands3 are16/3 and5. Delayed variant gives interval[3,6], worker payoffs3/5, cost2 and net output4.

checks.result: Adding IC yields monotone quantities, and the fee bounds follow from low IR and high IC with the correct payment direction. Attaining both bounds satisfies the other two restrictions. The reduced objective is strictly concave for0<lambda<1; the stationary high quantity thetaH and clipped low quantity satisfy monotonicity, so no omitted constraint invalidates the claimed global optimum. The feasible reduction includes pooling and exclusion. Weak intended-choice ties are disclosed, and strict epsilon fees approach the baseline profit without claiming exact strong implementation.
checks.independent_calculation: Without using the manuscript's fee or quantity formulas, represented the four original IC/IR inequalities as linear halfspaces in (tL,tH). Enumerated all pairwise boundary intersections, retained feasible payment vertices and scored profit directly. Searched all1,369 quantity pairs (qL,qH) on{0,1/3,...,12}^2 for each of three cases, including nonmonotone pairs whose fee regions were infeasible. The unique sampled optimum in each case reproduced baseline quantities(2,8), fees(8,56), profit12; transfer quantities(5/3,7), fees(5,127/3), profit43/6; exclusion quantities(0,8), fees(0,64), profit64/3. This is an independent finite diagnostic; the reviewed concavity argument establishes global continuous optimality.
